name: Metal
blurb: Riff metal: downpicked power-chord chugs and gallops on a hard grid, a pick bass locked in unison with the kick, and dark aeolian leads over a static low root.

flavors.label: Downtuned Chug
flavors.blurb: One root, palm-muted to death — the riff is the song and it never leaves home.

flavors.label: Phrygian Slam
flavors.blurb: Groove-metal breakdown: the b2 lands like a door slamming, then back to the low root.

flavors.label: Gallop Anthem
flavors.blurb: NWOBHM ride-out — i-bVI-bVII power chords ringing over a gallop.

flavors.label: Doom Crawl
flavors.blurb: Half the speed, none of the muting: open chords left to ring and decay.

flavors.label: Neoclassical Cadence
flavors.blurb: Harmonic minor with a real major V7 pulling home — the shred-era cadence.

arranger.llmStyleBrief: Metal harmony is riff-first and almost always aeolian or phrygian minor: a static i pedal doing the work, with bIII, bVI and bVII as the moving weight and the b2 as the slam. Power chords and triads, never maj7. Changes are slow, one or two a loop, landing hard on the downbeat with the kick. Only cadence: harmonic-minor V7.
